messages:
incident-bot: Paging: org delta-scale exceeding org QPS threshold (90th p95 latency > 1.8s). Trigger: org-qps-spike. Pager: oncall-alex. See dashboard: https://console.redwood/alerts/4924
oncall-alex: Acknowledged. Looking. Any obvious root cause or deploy? :eyes:
sre-jaya: Seeing a sustained pattern of short burst requests from delta-scale user agents — mostly embedding + long-chat sessions. Errors climbing from 0.2% -> 2.7% in last 6m. CPU burn on their dedicated pool hitting 92%.
eng-infra-miguel: No recent deploys in that fleet. I can temporarily raise org rate cap if we want to keep them alive while we triage. Recommend 2x org QPS for 60m and enable request-sampling for heavy calls.
oncall-alex: What's impact to other customers if we bump?
sre-jaya: If we bump delta-scale, global pool backlog increases but will remain under soft global RL. We should also disable the beta bulk-summarize feature for non-enterprise customers to reduce tail. That will cut their heavy requests by ~35%.
support-kate: I'll ring in support and prepare a status note if we do a config change. Do we want a short customer-facing message?
sales-lin: I'll ping DeltaScale account team. We need to be careful with commercial terms; but we can provide a heads-up. If you bump rate, they might keep sending — coordinate with them to throttle client-side.
oncall-alex: Miguel, execute the bump. Post the exact command you run so we can trace it.
eng-infra-miguel: Running: `redwoodctl rate adjust --org delta-scale --qps 240 --duration 3600 --reason "emergency spike mitigation"`
incident-bot: Action logged: rate.adjust by eng-infra-miguel at 4924681389. New org QPS=240 TTL=3600s.
sre-jaya: Metrics look stabilizing. 1m latency down from 1.9s -> 1.1s, errors down to 0.9%. We'll keep sampling heavy requests and surface slow traces to the thread.
oncall-alex: Support note draft: "We're seeing a high-volume traffic spike from DeltaScale affecting their requests. We've applied a temporary QPS increase for 60 minutes while we triage. We'll follow up with mitigations and a timeline for rollback." Kate please send if approved.
support-kate: Draft sent to #support-digest, tagging account team.
sales-lin: Noted. I'll ask them to reduce client-side concurrency and check whether this is an ETL job gone rogue. If they need extra capacity, we should discuss contract changes after incident.
sre-jaya: Quick check: bulk-summarize toggle rolled back for non-Enterprise: `feature-toggle set bulk-summarize false --scope non-enterprise` — applied at 4924681398. Bot will log.
incident-bot: Feature toggle event recorded. bulk-summarize disabled for non-enterprise at 4924681398 by sre-jaya.
eng-infra-miguel: Monitoring queue length and kernel utilization; will roll back bump if global backlog grows > 150k tokens. Current global backlog stable.
oncall-alex: I'm going to hand this to daytime oncall at 4924681400 — @sre-jaya you stay on triage and escalate to Platform Eng if patterns persist. Handoff note: temp QPS=240 until 4924684989 (1 hour), bulk-summarize disabled for non-Enterprise, customer notified.
sre-jaya: Ack. I'll open Incident runbook entry and create a follow-up ticket to investigate root cause and recommend long-term throttles/alerts.
support-kate: Customer acknowledged via account team, they say they're investigating a runaway job. Will push them to rate-limit client side.
sales-lin: I'll coordinate a postmortem touchpoint with DeltaScale AM.
oncall-alex: Closing my page. If anything degrades, please re-page SRE pager. :thumbsup:
eng-infra-miguel: Will auto-revoke bump at TTL expiry; I'll also prepare a safe rollback command: `redwoodctl rate adjust --org delta-scale --qps 120 --duration 0 --reason "rollback after spike"`
sre-jaya: Adding notes to incident tracker: https://issues.redwood/INC-4924. Postmortem owner: jaya.
support-kate: Leaving follow-ups in support queue.
sales-lin: Thx team. Keep me posted if we need a customer credit discussion.
incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated. Monitoring. Logs and action history attached to INC-4924.
